title: Brane cluster gases and ghost-free form factors for quantum gravity: verification suite and figure scripts
description:
Source, verification suites and figure scripts for two manuscripts by Deep Bhattacharjee, prepared for Physical Review D.

Brane cluster gases and ghost-free form factors for quantum gravity (paper/, code/). The suite checks_clusters.py runs 171 independent checks in eleven groups: the nerve complex and its Euler identity, intersection numbers on the torus, the subset-sum and Poisson generating functions, the Barnes-Rivers projector algebra, the residue sum rule and the pole dichotomy, the superficial degree of divergence, the Euclidean propagator of the Gaussian form factor in D = 3, 4, 5, 6, the Newtonian potential and the weak-field threshold, the on-shell dispersion relation, the Schwinger parametric representation with its spanning-tree bound and the closed-form one-loop bubble, and the composition of transmission amplitudes against the exact transfer matrix. The eight figure scripts regenerate every figure at 600 dpi and run a label collision test before saving.

Finite quantum gravity from a scale-invariant gas of branes (uv-finite/, new in 2.0.0). Every result of this paper is derived analytically in the text; the code only re-evaluates the formulas. verify.py runs 195 checks (Python, with numpy, scipy and mpmath): the single-brane factor of the cell model, the entire exponential integral and its bounds, the form factor of one realization of the Poisson gas and its closed-form fluctuation statistics, Monte Carlo samples of the gas, the necessity of fine graining, the vertex bound and power counting, the one-loop pole matrix of the quartic operators, the Mellin-transform vacuum energy, the one-loop bubble and its cutting rule, and the Newtonian potential. formfactor_check.c runs 84 checks of the same formulas in C99 with its own special functions. verify.jl runs 114 checks in Julia, in 256-bit arithmetic with its own special functions, quadrature and Monte Carlo, and checks the angular averages exactly in rational arithmetic. PowerCounting.lean proves in Lean 4 the integer statements behind the power counting and the one-loop tuning: the merging inequality, the bound on the superficial degree, its sign for all n ≥ 4 and L ≥ 2 and for every fine graining the paper allows, and the determinants and tuning of the pole matrix. make_figures.py regenerates the twelve plotted figures.
